<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917648_theRebbe_921" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917648_theRebbe_921__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the famous question of why the Torah begins with Bereishis rather than the first commandment, and resolves it by explaining that the Torah's purpose is to draw down the infinite light of Ein Sof into the lowest realms, including the narrative of Creation, in order to refine the inheritance of the nations and make a dwelling place for G-d.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is in the manner of what our sages said, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="3">"The Torah should not have begun except from 'This month is for you,' etc. And what is the reason it opened with Bereishis? Because of 'the strength of His works He declared to His people, to give them the inheritance of the nations.'</t>
    <t s="4">For if the nations of the world say to Israel, 'You are robbers, for you conquered the lands of the seven nations,'</t>
    <t s="5">they say to them, 'All the earth belongs to the Holy One, blessed is He;</t>
    <t s="6">He created it and gave it to whomever is upright in His eyes.</t>
    <t s="7">By His will He gave it to them, and by His will He took it from them and gave it to us.'"</t>
    <t s="8">And the precise point in this is known,</t>
    <t s="9">for seemingly, the question is that the Torah should not have begun except from "This month is for you,"</t>
    <t s="10">even though "In the beginning G-d created," etc., is the root of faith,</t>
    <t s="11">[so that] the matter of the Maaseh Bereishis (the Work of Creation)</t>
    <t s="12">(and likewise all the matters after this until the portion of HaChodesh)</t>
    <t s="13">would be transmitted orally,</t>
    <t s="14">or would be written in a separate book</t>
    <t s="15">(and not in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="16">for since the matter of the Torah is commandments and instructions for Israel,</t>
    <t s="17">therefore it should begin with the first commandment with which Israel was commanded),</t>
    <t s="18">and what is the answer "because of the strength of His works," etc.?</t>
    <t s="19">For even when the matter of Maaseh Bereishis would be transmitted orally,</t>
    <t s="20">Israel would know how to respond to the claim of the nations of the world.</t>
    <t s="21">And also it requires explanation,</t>
    <t s="22">for the Torah is above the world,</t>
    <t s="23">and how can it be said that in order to answer the nations of the world there would be a change in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="24">that it begins with Bereishis,</t>
    <t s="25">even though from the perspective of the matter of the Torah its beginning should be "This month is for you"?</t>
    <t s="26">And the point of the explanation in this is,</t>
    <t s="27">that this [idea] that the Torah should not have begun except from "This month is for you" is,</t>
    <t s="28">because all the revelations that were until the Exodus from Egypt</t>
    <t s="29">(which are discussed in the portions before the portion of HaChodesh)</t>
    <t s="30">are from the light that relates to the worlds</t>
    <t s="31">(as above in section 3),</t>
    <t s="32">and the matter of the Torah is the drawing down and revelation of the Ein Sof light, blessed and distinguished, which is above any relation to the worlds.</t>
    <t s="33">Therefore, the Torah should not have begun except from "This month is for you," which relates to the Exodus from Egypt, when the revelation of the Ein Sof that is above relation to the worlds began.</t>
    <t s="34">But nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="35">since the intention of the Torah is to draw down the revelation of the Ein Sof light, blessed and distinguished, within the limitation of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="36">and specifically in the lowest matters,</t>
    <t s="37">therefore the Torah also contains the narrative of Maaseh Bereishis</t>
    <t s="38">(and likewise the other portions before the portion of HaChodesh),</t>
    <t s="39">in order</t>
    <t s="40">to draw down the blessed and distinguished [light] of the Torah also into the</t>
    <t s="41">(because)</t>
    <t s="42">lowest matters,</t>
    <t s="43">and to make in them a dwelling place for Him, blessed is He.</t>
    <t s="44">And this is that it opened with Bereishis because of "the strength of His works He declared to His people, to give them the inheritance of the nations,"</t>
    <t s="45">for this, that the Torah contains the narrative of Maaseh Bereishis</t>
    <t s="46">(even though that which is revealed in creation is only a constricted illumination,</t>
    <t s="47">and as is explained in the maamar</t>
    <t s="48">at length, the reason for the statement "I am the L-rd your G-d who brought you out of the land of Egypt" and not "who created the heavens and the earth")</t>
    <t s="49">is,</t>
    <t s="50">because the ultimate intention of the Torah is that Israel will also refine the inheritance of the nations and make it into the Land of Israel,</t>
    <t s="51">and that the refinement will be in such a manner that even the nations of the world will agree to it,</t>
    <t s="52">for which reason Israel needs to answer the nations of the world</t>
    <t s="53">regarding their claim.</t>
    <t s="54">And this is also one of the reasons for this, that it opened with Bereishis,</t>
    <t s="55">for the perfection of the dwelling place in the lower realms is that the lower realm, from its own perspective, becomes a vessel for G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="56">and this matter is specifically through the refinement that is in the manner of enclothing,</t>
    <t s="57">in a manner of from below to above,</t>
    <t s="58">and therefore</t>
    <t s="59">the order of the events in the Torah</t>
    <t s="60">(for through the study of these matters in the Torah, refinement is accomplished)</t>
    <t s="61">is in a manner of from below to above,</t>
    <t s="62">the narrative of Maaseh Bereishis</t>
    <t s="63">(which includes the refinement of the inheritance of the nations),</t>
    <t s="64">and afterwards the narrative of the deeds of the Patriarchs, etc.,</t>
    <t s="65">and only after this — "This month is for you."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the purpose of the primordial tzimtzum (contraction) was ultimately for the sake of a greater revelation, analogous to how the inheritance of the nations was given to them initially so that it could be taken and given to Israel, achieving a higher level.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter in more detail will be understood based on what is stated in several discourses</t>
    <t s="2">(regarding the matter of "the Torah should not have begun except from 'This month is for you,' and what is the reason it opened with Bereishis"),</t>
    <t s="3">that it is stated in the Emek HaMelech at its beginning that the creation and coming into being of the worlds was through the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="4">for the matter of the tzimtzum</t>
    <t s="5">(the first tzimtzum)</t>
    <t s="6">is that the light that shone initially became completely concealed,</t>
    <t s="7">and through this a void and empty space was made for the existence of the worlds.</t>
    <t s="8">And the intention of the tzimtzum is</t>
    <t s="9">in order that through the Torah and mitzvos there will be the revelation of the Ein Sof also in the worlds.</t>
    <t s="10">For before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="11">when the Ein Sof light filled the void,</t>
    <t s="12">it was impossible for the existence of the worlds to be,</t>
    <t s="13">and there was no revelation in the worlds,</t>
    <t s="14">and through the tzimtzum it was innovated that the revelation of the Ein Sof would also be in the worlds.</t>
    <t s="15">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="16">that through this there will also be the revelation of the innerness of the Ein Sof, which is above even the light that shone before the tzimtzum.</t>
    <t s="17">And it is understood from this,</t>
    <t s="18">that the same applies regarding this that "by His will He gave it to them,"</t>
    <t s="19">for the intention in this from the outset is in order that there should be "by His will He took it from them and gave it to us,"</t>
    <t s="20">and through this, that the inheritance of the nations is transformed into the Land of Israel, it is elevated most greatly.</t>
    <t s="21">And through studying in the Torah "In the beginning G-d created,"</t>
    <t s="22">that the creation of the worlds was through the tzimtzum and concealment of the Name Elokim</t>
    <t s="23">(beginning from the first tzimtzum),</t>
    <t s="24">through this they reveal the secret of the tzimtzum, that the intention of the tzimtzum is for the sake of revelation.</t>
    <t s="25">And the same applies regarding the diminution of the moon,</t>
    <t s="26">the sin of the Tree of Knowledge, etc.</t>
    <t s="27">[And as is known,</t>
    <t s="28">that the tzimtzum and the breaking of the vessels of Tohu and the diminution of the moon and the sin of the Tree of Knowledge are related to each other],</t>
    <t s="29">for through studying these matters in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="30">the inner intention within them is revealed,</t>
    <t s="31">which was for the sake of revelation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section clarifies that the inclusion of the Creation narrative in the Torah is not a change or foreign element, because after the revelation of the Exodus and the Giving of the Torah, this narrative reveals the inner purpose of the tzimtzum, making it truly Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this it will also be understood that the writing in the Torah of the narrative of Maaseh Bereishis</t>
    <t s="2">(because of "the strength of His works He declared to His people, to give them the inheritance of the nations")</t>
    <t s="3">is not, heaven forbid, a change in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="4">that in order for Israel to know how to answer the nations of the world, other matters that are not Torah were written in the Torah, heaven forbid,</t>
    <t s="5">for this, that the matter of Maaseh Bereishis is a tzimtzum of the Name Elokim</t>
    <t s="6">(and therefore it does not relate to the Torah, which is the revelation of the Name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="7">the revelation of the Ein Sof light, blessed and distinguished)</t>
    <t s="8">is as it is in itself,</t>
    <t s="9">before the revelation of the Exodus from Egypt and the Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="10">But after there was the revelation of the Exodus from Egypt and the Giving of the Torah</t>
    <t s="11">("This month is for you"),</t>
    <t s="12">and the matter of Maaseh Bereishis is written in the Torah to reveal the inner intention of the tzimtzum</t>
    <t s="13">(in order that through this there will be a more elevated revelation),</t>
    <t s="14">behold, the revelation of the inner intention of the tzimtzum is like all the matters in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">for despite being enclothed in physical things, they are Torah,</t>
    <t s="16">the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed is He, which is above the world,</t>
    <t s="17">and this, that it descended and became enclothed in physical things, is in order</t>
    <t s="18">to draw down the blessed and distinguished [light] of the Torah also below.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
